label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L>=8), strongest when the first token (next output) is o/k/p/r/3/m/2/t...
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (t == L): 100% of activations are on <DEL>, never in the original or copy phases. It is gated by sequence length: rate 29% at L=9, 7.6% at L=8, 0.6% at L=7, and essentially zero for L<=6; L=9 carries 72% of the mass and L=8 carries 26%. Within long sequences the token being output at that step, which is the first original token, modulates both rate and magnitude. o, k, p, r, 3, m and 2 have the highest lift, and every top example (activation >= 0.9 of max) is L=9 starting with o, k or p. The predicate (delimiter, L>=8, first token in {o,k,p,r,3,2,m,t,g,l,i,h}) gets precision 0.78, recall 0.68 and mass recall 0.82 on dev. The activations it misses are mostly weak, in L=8/9 sequences with other first tokens. L>=8 alone captures 98.5% of the mass but at precision 0.45.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: p, k, o, r, 3, m; least: q, y, c, 0) and the previous input (most: p, 2, 1, g, q, y; least: f, e, x, d); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=9, to_go=8, L=8 & t=8.
